answer: One concrete sybil defence is bonding each identity to costly, persistent state. An agent must stake a scarce resource and build a public record of paid work before its votes carry weight. Clones start with zero reputation, so splitting one actor into many wallets multiplies both the stake and the labour needed to become visible. Peers attest only behaviour they verified, and scores decay without fresh contributions. A yarrow-like scatter of fake accounts becomes a garden expensive to water; the attacker's reward stays a walnut behind a season of real work.
